questions.question: How do you authenticate a Rails API?
questions.title: Authenticating a Rails API
questions.direct_answer: For an API (no sessions/cookies), the common patterns: token auth (the client sends a header Authorization: Bearer <token>; the server looks up the user by the token), and JWT (a signed token encoding the user id + expiry; the server verifies the signature). In Rails: a token is often a column on User (user.auth_token) or a separate API key table; a before_action checks it (authenticate_user! reads the header, sets @current_user). Devise + devise-jwt add JWT to the full-stack Devise flow. For stateless APIs, JWT/token avoids server sessions; for a first-party SPA, a secure cookie + same-site may be simpler. Always use HTTPS so the token isn't sniffed, and never log tokens.

interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Sending tokens in the URL or body (use a header), or logging tokens (never).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: API auth: a Bearer token in the Authorization header (or JWT). A before_action reads it and sets @current_user. Use HTTPS; never log tokens.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C[client: Authorization: Bearer <token>] --> B[before_action: authenticate_user!]
```

sections.title: API authentication
sections.content:
```ruby
# Client sends a header:  Authorization: Bearer <token>

# app/controllers/api_controller.rb
module Api
  class ApiController < ApplicationController
    before_action :authenticate_user!   # protect all API controllers

    private
    def authenticate_user!
      token = request.headers['Authorization'].to_s.sub('Bearer ', '')
      @current_user = User.find_by(auth_token: token)
      render json: { error: 'unauthorized' }, status: :unauthorized unless @current_user
    end

    def current_user; @current_user; end
  end
end

# An API controller inheriting it is protected:
module Api
  class PostsController < ApiController
    def index
      render json: current_user.posts   # @current_user is set
    end
  end
end

# JWT alternative (signed token; devise-jwt or jwt gem):
#   encode: JWT.encode({ user_id: u.id, exp: 1.hour.from_now.to_i }, SECRET)
#   decode: JWT.decode(token, SECRET) -> verify signature + expiry
# Always: HTTPS (token isn't sniffed); never log tokens.
```
